narrative:
The model has analyzed your academic situation and determined that there’s a **25% chance** you might not pass your final year—that’s higher than the 10% threshold that triggers this warning. While this doesn’t mean failure is certain, it does mean the system is strongly advising you to take extra steps now to improve your chances.

The biggest reason for this recommendation comes from **how your past academic performance compares to your current challenges**. You haven’t had any prior class failures, which actually works in your favor—this is the strongest positive factor in your case. However, two other key aspects are pulling the prediction toward a higher risk of struggling.

First, your **father’s level of education** stands out as a significant factor. Most students who don’t need remedial courses come from families where at least one parent has completed secondary education or higher. Since your father’s education level is lower than average among students who are doing well, this creates additional hurdles—likely because academic support at home may be less available.

Second, while your **aspiration to pursue higher education** is a strong motivator (and most students share this goal), the model notes that without extra support, this ambition alone isn’t enough to overcome other challenges you’re facing. Many students who succeed balance their studies with family help, paid tutoring, or structured study time—areas where your situation differs from the majority of those who pass without extra intervention.

You’re also dealing with **longer travel times to school** (30-60 minutes daily) and **limited weekly study time** (less than 2 hours), which are far below what most successful students invest. Combined with **seven school absences**—more than double the average—this suggests you may be struggling to keep up with the workload.

To turn this around, focus on **increasing your study time**, seeking **additional academic support** (either from family or paid tutors), and **reducing absences** to catch up on missed work. The model isn’t saying you’ll fail—it’s giving you a clear heads-up so you can take action before it’s too late.
